overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a dominant viewer preference for space and planetary 'What If' scenarios, particularly extreme environments involving bizarre physics, exotic materials, and celestial oddities. Videos framed around hypothetical falls into extreme planets (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice) and rare planetary anomalies consistently achieve the highest velocity in views-per-day and strong engagement (likes-per-view). Conversely, psychological and biological trivia from older datasets show lower baseline momentum.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generate over 1,000 views rapidly with strong like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios involving newly discovered or bizarre exoplanets.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring counterintuitive facts about celestial bodies—such as Venus having a day longer than its year (A9Qa-RmuOr0) or TrES-2b being darker than coal (v1rrcZLdp4U)—pull high initial traction and strong retention hooks.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing cosmic anomaly contrasts that challenge common perceptions of physics and time.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) and brain memory loops (5AN7LUgqarc) show stagnant view counts below 80 views after extended periods.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological life-hacks in favor of tangible, high-visual-potential space and physics concepts.
